Understanding Revisional Eyelid Surgery

Revisional eyelid surgery, also known as secondary eyelid surgery, is performed to address complications or unsatisfactory results from a previous eyelid surgery. Common issues that may necessitate revisional surgery include:

Excessive Scarring

Visible scars that affect the appearance or function of the eyelids.

Asymmetry

Uneven or unbalanced eyelid appearance.

Incomplete Correction

Persistent drooping, puffiness, or other issues not fully addressed by the initial surgery.

Overcorrection

Excessive removal of skin or fat, leading to a hollow or tight appearance.

Functional Problems

Issues with eyelid movement, closure, or vision.

The Revisional Eyelid Surgery Procedure

Revisional eyelid surgery is a highly individualized procedure tailored to address each patient’s unique concerns. During your consultation, our surgeons will:

Thorough Evaluation

Conduct a comprehensive assessment of your eyelids, including a review of your surgical history and current concerns.

Customized Surgical Plan

Develop a detailed plan to address the specific issues identified, using advanced techniques to achieve optimal results.

Surgical Procedure

Perform the surgery with precision, focusing on minimizing scarring and maximizing aesthetic and functional improvements.

Post-Operative Care

Provide detailed aftercare instructions to ensure a smooth recovery and the best possible outcomes.

Healing and Recovery

Recovery from revisional eyelid surgery varies depending on the complexity of the procedure. Most patients experience:

Mild Swelling and Bruising

These symptoms typically subside within one to two weeks.

Minimal Discomfort

Pain is usually minimal and can be managed with prescribed medications.

Return to Normal Activities

Most patients can resume their regular routines within 10-14 days.

The final results will become more apparent as swelling decreases, revealing a smoother, more symmetrical, and natural-looking eyelid appearance.

Frequently Asked Questions | Revisional Eyelid Surgery

What Issues Can Revisional Eyelid Surgery Correct?

Revisional eyelid surgery can address a range of issues, including excessive scarring, asymmetry, incomplete correction, overcorrection, and functional problems resulting from previous eyelid surgery.

How Soon After My Initial Surgery Can I Have Revisional Eyelid Surgery?

It is generally recommended to wait at least six months to one year after your initial surgery before undergoing revisional eyelid surgery. This allows sufficient time for healing and assessment of the final results.

Is Revisional Eyelid Surgery More Complex Than the Initial Surgery?

Revisional eyelid surgery can be more complex due to the presence of scar tissue and the need to correct previous surgical outcomes. It requires a high level of expertise and precision, which our experienced oculoplastic surgeons at AestheticEye are well-equipped to provide.

What Are the Risks Associated with Revisional Eyelid Surgery?

As with any surgical procedure, there are potential risks, including infection, bleeding, and complications related to anesthesia. However, these risks are minimized when the surgery is performed by experienced oculoplastic surgeons like Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament at AestheticEye.

How Can I Ensure the Best Results from Revisional Eyelid Surgery?

Choosing a qualified and experienced oculoplastic surgeon is crucial for achieving the best results. Following post-operative care instructions and attending follow-up appointments are also essential for a successful outcome.

Will My Insurance Cover Revisional Eyelid Surgery?

Insurance coverage for revisional eyelid surgery varies. If the surgery is medically necessary to correct functional issues, it may be covered. Cosmetic revisions are typically not covered by insurance. Our team can help you navigate your insurance options during your consultation.
